initial_prompt: Write me a regex that validates email addresses according to RFC 5321.

messages.content: Write me a regex that validates email addresses according to RFC 5321.

# RFC 5321 Email Validation Regex

**Honest caveat first**: A regex that *fully* validates RFC 5321 is essentially impossible—the spec allows for quoted strings, nested comments, and other constructs that push beyond what regular expressions can cleanly handle. What I can provide is a regex that covers the vast majority of real-world valid addresses while being reasonably faithful to the spec.

## Practical RFC 5321-Compliant Regex

```regex
^(?:[a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*|"(?:[\x20-\x21\x23-\x5B\x5D-\x7E]|\\[\x20-\x7E])*")@(?:(?:[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}|\[(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\])$
```

## Breakdown

### Local Part (before @)
```
(?:
  [a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+          # dot-atom text
  (?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*   # more dot-atom segments
  |
  "(?:[\x20-\x21\x23-\x5B\x5D-\x7E]|\\[\x20-\x7E])*"  # quoted string
)
```

### Domain Part (after @)
```
(?:
  (?:[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+  # domain labels
  [a-zA-Z]{2,}                                      # TLD
  |
  \[(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\.){3}  # IP literal
  (?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\]
)
```

## What This Handles
- ✅ Standard addresses: `user@example.com`
- ✅ Dots in local part: `first.last@example.com`
- ✅ Special characters: `user+tag@example.com`
- ✅ Quoted strings: `"unusual@chars"@example.com`
- ✅ IP literals: `user@[192.168.1.1]`

## What This Doesn't Handle
- ❌ Comments (obsolete syntax)
- ❌ IPv6 address literals
- ❌ Non-ASCII (internationalized) email addresses (RFC 6531)

## Practical Recommendation

For most applications, this simpler version is sufficient and easier to maintain:

```regex
^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$
```

**Best practice**: Use regex for basic format checking, then verify deliverability by actually sending a confirmation email.
